title: Homotopy invariance from bounded-below quasi-isomorphism inversion
statement: Let C be an abelian category and D a category. Consider integer-indexed cochain complexes in C, with differentials raising degree by one. A complex is strictly bounded below if all its terms below some integer are zero. Let H be a functor from these cochain complexes to D which sends every quasi-isomorphism between strictly bounded-below complexes to an isomorphism. For any strictly bounded-below complexes K and L and homotopic chain maps f,g from K to L, H(f)=H(g). Here a quasi-isomorphism is a chain map inducing isomorphisms on all homology objects, and a chain homotopy is a degree-minus-one family whose differential is the difference of the chain maps.

source.place: Tag 09A2, homotopy invariance in the bounded-below hypercover comparison; elementary cylinder argument

proof.text: Choose a lower bound n for K. The cylinder of K is zero in degrees below n-1, since its degree q consists of two copies of K in degree q and one shifted copy in degree q+1. Thus the cylinder is again strictly bounded below. This also covers zero complexes and arbitrary lower bounds.

The cylinder projection to K is a homotopy equivalence, hence a quasi-isomorphism between strictly bounded-below complexes. Its image under H is invertible. Both cylinder inclusions compose with this projection to the identity, so cancellation shows that their images under H coincide.
A homotopy from f to g yields a map from the cylinder to L whose composites with the two inclusions are f and g. Apply H and the equality of the images of the inclusions to conclude H(f)=H(g).

lean.statement:
theorem map_eq_of_boundedBelow_homotopy
    {C : Type*} [Category* C] [Abelian C] {D : Type*} [Category* D]
    (H : CochainComplex C ℤ ⥤ D)
    (hH : ∀ (K L : CochainComplex.Plus C) (f : K ⟶ L),
      QuasiIso f.hom → IsIso (H.map f.hom))
    (K L : CochainComplex.Plus C) (f g : K.obj ⟶ L.obj) (h : Homotopy f g) :
    H.map f = H.map g
